Short Quizzes Before Lectures

Some instructors give short quizzes before lectures to encourage students to complete the reading. Are pre-lecture quizzes a good way to improve learning? Explain your opinion with reasons and examples.

Aria: Pre-lecture quizzes can be useful because they push students to read before class and notice confusing points early. However, the quizzes should be low-stakes, or students may focus on memorizing details instead of preparing thoughtful questions.

Joon: I think these quizzes work best when they are connected to discussion. If the teacher reviews common wrong answers, students can see why the reading matters, but a quiz that only records a score may not improve understanding much.
